title: AURA: Visually Interpretable Affective Understanding via Robust Archetypes
claim: A self-organizing archetype space replaces text proxies and fixed prototypes, supporting classification, detection and regression through one visual pipeline.
layout: 2 halves: training pipeline left, three stacked inference comparisons right; left-to-right flow
description: A wide two-part figure. The left 'Training Stage' shows face datasets (AU, FER, VA) and a single face photo feeding a frozen CLIP visual encoder, then a VAS projector. The projector output goes into a rounded 'Visual Archetype Space' panel with colored star-shaped clusters of face thumbnails and scattered dots, above a row of colored archetype tokens with loss terms, a prediction head and regularization. An orange 'Archetype Contextualization' column holds gated fusion, distance-aware contextualization and a semantic token projector. The right 'Inference Stage' has three stacked gray or blue panels: Our AURA with adaptive density, prototype/cluster approaches with fixed density, and CLIP text-image matching with handcrafted or learned prompts. Green checks and red crosses mark which tasks each approach handles.
caption: Overview of AURA. Left: Training stage. AURA supports FER, AU detection, and VA regression through three components: a Visual Archetype-Space Projector that maps frozen CLIP features into a task-specific archetype space, Self-organized Archetype Discovery
abstract: Interpretable methods such as vision--language models (VLMs) have advanced affect analysis by aligning images with textual descriptions. However, relying on text as an intermediate proxy faces critical limitations: linguistic templates are inherently discrete, making them fundamentally incompatible with continuous valence--arousal regression, while also acting as a bottleneck for fine-grained visual nuances. Cognitive psychology suggests that human affective perception is not mediated by linguistic translation, but is grounded in perceptual resemblance to internalized visual archetypes. Motivated by this, we propose AURA, an archetype-based framework that replaces brittle linguistic proxies with a self-organizing archetype manifold. By adaptively allocating representational density according to affective complexity, AURA enables accurate continuous regression and reshapes affective taxonomies by decomposing labels into interpretable, geometrically coherent visual primitives. This paradigm offers a transparent, visually grounded decision trail and achieves state-of-the-art results across discrete and continuous tasks.
